title: Test-run fan-in: the "Settle it" hint names `recover`, which another repository's launcher may lack, and "Interrupted: no" contradicts an UNKNOWN (process gone) verdict
outcome:
The termal_resume_after_test_runs fan-in prompt (test_run_card_lines, src/test_run_waits.rs:205-287) has two problems with an UNKNOWN verdict:
- It always adds "Settle it: `node scripts/test-launcher.mjs recover \"RUN_DIR\"`" (line 283). TermAl's own launcher has `recover`, but runs are watched in other repositories too. Engram's launcher at cee0612 has no such subcommand and answers "usage: test-launcher.mjs full|focused … | summary|notify RUN_DIR".
- "Interrupted: yes|no" (line 217) prints the summary's interrupted flag, which comes only from terminal results. For a run whose process is gone and whose heartbeat is stale, with no terminal result, it prints "no" beside "Verdict: UNKNOWN (process gone)", which reads as a contradiction.
acceptance: For a run with no terminal result (UNKNOWN verdict), the Interrupted line says unknown rather than no; a test covers the process-gone case

The fan-in names a settle command only when the run's repository launcher offers it (or names it conditionally, e.g. `summary` everywhere and `recover` where available), so the hint never names a subcommand the launcher rejects; a test covers a run whose launcher has no `recover`
